sections.title: Trust in God Alone
observations: The psalmist begins by expressing his deep trust in God as his refuge and salvation. This sets the tone for the entire chapter, emphasizing the importance of relying solely on God in times of trouble.
The repetition of the phrase 'my soul' indicates a personal and intimate relationship with God, highlighting the psalmist's reliance on Him for strength and security.

sections.title: The Futility of Human Power
observations: In this section, the psalmist contrasts the stability found in God with the instability of human power and wealth. He acknowledges that even the most powerful individuals can be deceptive and unreliable.
This serves as a reminder to the reader that placing trust in human beings or material possessions is ultimately futile.

sections.title: God's Steadfast Love and Justice
observations: The psalmist reflects on God's character, emphasizing His steadfast love and justice. This reinforces the idea that God is not only a refuge but also a righteous judge who cares for His people.
The assurance of God's love provides comfort and hope, encouraging believers to remain steadfast in their faith.

importantVerses.commentary: For God alone my soul waits in silence; from him comes my salvation.
For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him.
Once God has spoken; twice have I heard this: that power belongs to God.

questions: What does it mean to wait in silence for God?
How can we practically apply the lesson of trusting in God over human power in our daily lives?
In what ways does understanding God's character as loving and just impact our faith and trust in Him?
